items.title: Hal Galper interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 27, 2022

ctx.x: You read a book that set you on this path, did you not?

Yes. And it’s interesting because in my first year at Berklee there were two things that preoccupied my mind and you have to understand I was totally naïve and totally ignorant of any musical knowledge. Two questions: what am I supposed to be feeling inside of me when I play? And, what is the nature of 1, the first beat of the bar? For some reason I had those two questions when I knew nothing. And those two questions have led me through everything that I’ve written and discovered about teaching and what the…

when Madam Chaloff, my technique teacher, I was working on a Bach piece and she made a phrases mark of an eighth note line starting on the second eighth note of the bar, going to the first eighth note to the next. A pencil marking, a phrase mark. When I saw that and everything moved towards the last note, that was the beginning of forward motion.
